security_properties.property: Contract code size check MUST occur AFTER init code execution completes and BEFORE deployment
security_properties.rationale: Checking at wrong time could allow oversized contracts to deploy or waste gas on checks before knowing final size

security_properties.property: Contract bytecode returned from init code MUST NOT exceed MAX_CODE_SIZE (24576 bytes) for successful deployment
security_properties.rationale: Exceeding limit could enable DoS attacks on light clients and unbounded state growth

security_properties.property: Code size exceeding 24576 bytes MUST trigger out-of-gas exception and consume all remaining gas
security_properties.rationale: Failing without gas penalty would make oversized deployment attempts cheap to spam

security_properties.property: Failed contract creation due to size limit MUST NOT create any contract at the target address
security_properties.rationale: Partial deployment could leave invalid contract state

security_properties.property: External deployer input MUST NOT bypass the code size validation check
security_properties.rationale: Bypassing validation would allow deployment of oversized contracts defeating DoS protection

security_properties.property: Code length measurement MUST accurately count all bytes in returned deployment bytecode
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect measurement could allow oversized contracts or reject valid ones

security_properties.property: Code length <= 24576 bytes MUST pass validation; length > 24576 bytes MUST fail validation
security_properties.rationale: Boundary condition clarity ensures consistent behavior at exactly 24576 bytes (AMB-EIP170-01)

security_properties.property: Size limit violation MUST consume ALL remaining gas, not just a portion
security_properties.rationale: Partial gas consumption could make oversized deployment attempts economically viable for attackers

security_properties.property: No gas refund SHALL be issued for failed contract creation due to size limit
security_properties.rationale: Refunds would reduce the cost of attack attempts

security_properties.property: Block validation MUST verify all contract creations satisfy the 24576 byte size limit
security_properties.rationale: Accepting blocks with oversized contracts would propagate invalid state

security_properties.property: Contract size limit MUST bound the verification time per block to prevent DoS on light clients
security_properties.rationale: Unbounded verification time enables DoS attacks where attackers deploy massive contracts

security_properties.property: Blocks received from P2P network MUST be validated for contract size limits before acceptance
security_properties.rationale: Accepting unvalidated blocks from untrusted peers could allow invalid state propagation

security_properties.property: MAX_CODE_SIZE limit MUST be consistently applied across all client implementations
security_properties.rationale: Inconsistent enforcement would cause consensus failures between clients (ASSUM-EIP170-01)

security_properties.property: At or after block 7,280,000 on mainnet, Petersburg consensus rules MUST be active
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect activation block would cause chain split with pre-Petersburg nodes

security_properties.property: Petersburg activation MUST disable EIP-1283 net gas metering for SSTORE operations
security_properties.rationale: Keeping EIP-1283 enabled would preserve the reentrancy attack vector

security_properties.property: Block number MUST be compared against Petersburg activation block BEFORE applying consensus rules
security_properties.rationale: Applying Petersburg rules to pre-activation blocks would break consensus with other nodes

security_properties.property: When Petersburg and Constantinople activate at the same block, Petersburg MUST take precedence
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect precedence would enable EIP-1283 and its reentrancy vulnerability

security_properties.property: Same-block activation MUST result in Constantinople features minus EIP-1283
security_properties.rationale: All other Constantinople features should remain active; only EIP-1283 is removed

security_properties.property: EIP-1283 net gas metering MUST be disabled to eliminate the reentrancy attack vector
security_properties.rationale: Cheap SSTORE operations enabled by EIP-1283 allow reentrancy attacks via insufficient transfer gas stipends

security_properties.property: After SSTORE pricing reversion, reentrancy attacks via transfer gas stipends MUST be economically infeasible
security_properties.rationale: Original SSTORE costs ensure 2300 gas stipend is insufficient for state-modifying reentrancy

security_properties.property: All client implementations MUST correctly implement fork precedence when Petersburg and Constantinople share activation block
security_properties.rationale: Incorrect precedence handling would cause consensus split between clients (ASSUM-EIP1716-01)

security_properties.property: Node operators MUST upgrade to Petersburg-aware clients BEFORE block 7,280,000
security_properties.rationale: Non-upgraded nodes will fork off on a separate chain with EIP-1283 enabled (ASSUM-EIP1716-02)

security_properties.property: eth_txGasLimitCap RPC method MUST return a QUANTITY (hex-encoded integer) or null
security_properties.rationale: Invalid response format could break wallet integrations and transaction construction

security_properties.property: Null response MUST indicate no finite gas limit cap exists
security_properties.rationale: Misinterpreting null could cause wallets to assume zero cap and reject all transactions

security_properties.property: RPC node responses MUST accurately reflect the effective gas cap
security_properties.rationale: Inaccurate cap information could cause transaction construction failures or invalid submissions

security_properties.property: Effective gas cap MUST be computed as min(protocolCap, policyCap)
security_properties.rationale: Using wrong formula could return cap higher than actually enforced, causing rejections

security_properties.property: When no protocol cap and no policy cap exist, method MUST return null
security_properties.rationale: Returning arbitrary value instead of null would mislead clients about actual limits

security_properties.property: Protocol cap (e.g., EIP-7825's 2^24) MUST be sourced from active protocol rules at query time
security_properties.rationale: Using outdated protocol cap after hard fork could cause valid transactions to be rejected

security_properties.property: Wallets MUST query gas cap BEFORE constructing transactions to avoid invalid submissions
security_properties.rationale: Constructing without knowing cap could result in rejected transactions and wasted user effort

security_properties.property: Transactions with estimated gas > cap MUST trigger user warning before submission
security_properties.rationale: Silent submission of over-cap transactions would result in rejections confusing users

security_properties.property: Gas estimation MUST be validated against discovered cap BEFORE user confirmation
security_properties.rationale: Post-confirmation validation would require re-confirmation and degrade UX

security_properties.property: User-provided transaction parameters from untrusted input MUST be validated against gas cap
security_properties.rationale: Accepting user input without validation could lead to invalid transaction construction

security_properties.property: Policy cap applies only to mempool admission, not consensus-level validation
security_properties.rationale: Transactions above policyCap but below protocolCap can still be included by other nodes (AMB-EIP8123-01)

security_properties.property: Clients SHOULD re-query gas cap after known hard forks to get current protocol cap
security_properties.rationale: Protocol cap may change at hard forks; stale values could cause transaction failures (AMB-EIP8123-02)

security_properties.property: RPC node MUST be trusted to return accurate cap information
security_properties.rationale: Malicious nodes could return incorrect caps causing transaction failures or misleading users (ASSUM-EIP8123-01)
